question: Who Owns Chick-fil-A?
quick_answer: Chick-fil-A is privately owned by the Cathy family. The first Chick-fil-A restaurant opened in 1967 at the Greenbriar Mall in Atlanta, Georgia, started by S. Truett Cathy, and the family has kept it private ever since, so it does not trade on any stock exchange. Leadership has stayed within the family, with Truett's son Dan Cathy serving as chairman.

body.heading: Who owns Chick-fil-A?
body.text: Chick-fil-A is owned by the Cathy family, who have kept the company private since it was founded. There are no outside shareholders and the chain has never had an IPO, so you cannot buy stock in Chick-fil-A. Control and leadership have stayed within the family across generations.

body.heading: The founder and the roots
body.text: S. Truett Cathy opened the first Chick-fil-A restaurant in 1967 at the Greenbriar Mall in Atlanta, Georgia. Years earlier he had run a small diner called the Dwarf Grill (later the Dwarf House) in Hapeville, just outside Atlanta, where he developed the chicken sandwich the brand is built on. After his passing, the family continued to lead the company, with his son Dan Cathy as chairman.

body.heading: How the restaurants are run
body.text: While the Cathy family owns the company, most Chick-fil-A restaurants are run by independent operators who are selected and licensed by the company. That model keeps the brand family-controlled at the top while local operators run day-to-day service.
